summary: Neo lies awake in bed when Tank enters, introduces himself as Neo's operator, and shakes his hand. Noticing Tank has no jacks, Neo stammers; Tank explains that he and his brother Dozer are pure 'home-grown human,' 'born free,' a 'genuine child of Zion.' When Neo asks what Zion is, Tank describes it as 'the last human city,' deep underground near the earth's core, and admits excitement about Neo's potential if Morpheus's belief is right, then urges they begin.

what_changes.before: Awake and staring at the lights, silent and unsure, he does not know who this newcomer is or what Zion means.
what_changes.after: He learns the man is his operator, that Zion is 'the last human city,' and that some humans are 'born free' without jacks.
what_changes.evidence: NEO / Zion? ... It's a city? ... The last human city. The only place we got left.

what_changes.before: A stranger stepping in unannounced, offering a handshake to a wary, sleepless Neo.
what_changes.after: He establishes kinship and reassurance by revealing shared humanity and excitement about Neo, closing with 'We got a lot to do so let's get to it.'
what_changes.evidence: Goddamn, I got to tell you, I'm fairly excited to see what you are capable of.

event_hint.one_line: Neo's operator Tank introduces himself and the concept of Zion, warming Neo up before training.

minds.wants: To find solid ground — any fact he can trust — in a reality that has just dissolved, and to gauge whether the person now in charge of his body is safe.
minds.feels: Raw and destabilized. He has not slept, has just vomited his way through the horror of waking from the pod (sc-044), and has been told by Morpheus that he cannot go back and is the fulfillment of a prophecy (sc-045). He is alone with a stranger who has no visible jacks, which violates the only model of 'human' he has ever had, and every answer Tank gives only opens a larger unknown (Zion, the war, 'born free').
minds.shows: Near-silence and short, stunned questions — 'No.', 'Zion?', 'It's a city?', 'Where is it?' — plus a broken-off observation ('You don't have...') that he cannot finish. He performs the ordinary social ritual of the handshake and lets himself be led, giving the appearance of a cooperative, if bewildered, recruit.
minds.basis: His 'No.' to 'Did you sleep?' and his fragment 'You don't have...' (a stated inability to complete the observation, handed to him on the page) followed by a chain of one- and two-word questions. The facts establish he 'does not know who this newcomer is or what Zion means' before, and learns these things after. sc-044/045 give the physiological and existential residue he is carrying into this room.

believes_about.belief: That Tank, as the man who will operate his connection to the Matrix and who is calmly explaining things, is a safe and trustworthy guide.
believes_about.wrong_because: Nothing yet justifies this trust beyond Tank's warmth; Neo is extrapolating safety from friendliness, and the whole world he has entered has already proven itself treacherous. This is the beginning of a trust that will later be betrayed from within the crew (Cipher), though Neo cannot know that.

believes_about.belief: That a human without jacks is a contradiction or a deformity — that jacks are what a person who interfaces with machines must have.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank is not deficient; he is 'born free,' a genuine child of Zion. Neo's entire frame of reference has been the Matrix, where everyone is jacked; he mistakes the exception for the anomaly.

minds.wants: To win Neo's trust and readiness quickly so training can begin, and to initiate this newcomer into the human world without frightening him off.
minds.feels: Genuinely excited and a little in awe — he is in the presence of the man Morpheus believes is the One, and he is, by his own account, barely containing it ('Goddamn... I'm fairly excited'). Underneath the buoyancy is the operator's practical urgency: there is a war, a prophecy riding this kid, and 'a lot to do.'
minds.shows: Warm, jokey, plainspoken hospitality — 'Morning. Did you sleep?', a handshake, self-deprecating humor about 'holes,' and a mythic, welcoming pitch about Zion ('where the party would be'). He deliberately withholds the forbidden talk ('We're not supposed to talk about any of that') while still letting his excitement leak through, and then closes the conversation down ('let's get to it') to convert wonder into momentum.
minds.basis: He volunteers kinship and reassurance (shared humanity, 'born free,' Zion as home), admits his excitement explicitly, flags the taboo around discussing the prophecy, and pivots to work. The trust-axis change in the facts ('establishes kinship and reassurance... closing with "We got a lot to do"') confirms the intent to warm Neo up.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is worth this excitement and can be warmed up through friendliness and a shared handshake — that he is, essentially, a receptive recruit who just needs orienting.
believes_about.wrong_because: He is underestimating how shattered Neo still is (sc-044's thrashing, the 'I can't go back' despair of sc-045). Neo is not merely uninformed; he is in shock and grieving a lost world, so Tank's buoyant salesmanship is aimed at a deeper wound than he registers.

believes_about.belief: That if Morpheus is right, this is straightforwardly 'an exciting time' — that sharing the awe will inspire Neo.
believes_about.wrong_because: The prophecy is a death sentence of responsibility, not a party; Neo has just been told he can never go back. Tank's framing assumes Neo shares his investment in the cause, when Neo has not yet consented to any of it.

connects_back: sc-044: Neo's violent unjacking and 'I don't believe it' collapse — this is the first human contact he has had since, and it is gentle by deliberate contrast.
sc-045: Morpheus's 'you can't go back' and the revelation that Neo may be the One — Tank now has to orient a man who knows he is trapped and is carrying a prophecy he did not ask for.
sc-045: Morpheus's 'Your training' — Tank's 'let's get to it' is the operational fulfillment of that closing line.
The Matrix-world model of the human body (everyone has jacks) that Neo carried his whole life, which makes Tank's jackless body read as impossible.
sets_up: ev-011: Tank's role as operator who manages Neo's physical connection is now established, making the orientation and the note about Neo's lack of jacks possible.
ev-012: The trust and rapport built here make it plausible that Tank, not a stranger, personally loads combat programs into Neo's port.
ev-013/ev-014: Neo's willingness to submit to brutal training rests on the operator-commander relationship this scene warms up.
The crew-intimacy arc (ev-015 Trinity's care) and the later betrayal from within the crew depend on this being a crew Neo has been made to feel at home with.
dramatic_function: To humanize the terrifying new reality by giving Neo — and the audience — a warm, funny, trustworthy human face, converting the abstract horror and prophecy of the previous scenes into a lived, relational world (Zion, 'born free,' kinship) so that the training to come feels like being guided rather than used.
